Rashi on Sotah 6a:10:1.hebrew: ואנהר לן עיינין - הביא לנו ראיה לדבריו ממתניתין:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:10:1.english: And he enlightened our eyes - He brought us proof for his statement from the Mishnah.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:10:2.hebrew: סוטה שיש לה עדים במדינת הים - שראו שנטמאה מזה:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:10:2.english: A sotah who has witnesses overseas - Who saw that she was defiled by this [man].

Rashi on Sotah 6a:10:3.hebrew: ועד אין בה - אע"ג דדרשינן לעיל לעד אחד נאמן בסוטה, ולסוטה ודאית שלא תשתה עוד, אין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו, ודרשינן ליה נמי הכי: ועד אין בה הוא דאמר "והביא האיש את אשתו" וכל הפרשה. הא יש בה עד — אין המים בודקין אותה:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:10:3.english: "And there is no witness against her" - Even though we expounded above [that the verse teaches] that one witness is believed regarding a sotah, and [that] a definite sotah does not drink any longer, a verse does not depart from its plain meaning, and we expound it also in this way: It is only when "there is no witness against her" that [the Torah] says "And the man shall bring his wife" and the entire passage. But if there is a witness against her, the waters do not test her.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:11:1.hebrew: ואנהרינהו לעיינין - משום דקרא לאו ראיה הוא כל כך, דהא דרשיניה לסוטה ודאית שיש בה עד אחד לפנינו, וללמד שלא תשתה:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:11:1.english: And he enlightened [our] eyes - Because the verse is not such a strong proof, since we expound it [as referring] to a definite sota, against whom there is one witness before us, and [as coming] to teach that she does not drink.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:11:2.hebrew: זונה היא - ופשיטא דאסורה בתרומה, דהא תנא ליה "האומרת טמאה אני":
Rashi on Sotah 6a:11:2.english: She is a zonah - And it is obvious that she is forbidden to eat terumah, for [the Mishnah] already taught, "She who says, 'I am defiled.'"

Rashi on Sotah 6a:12:1.hebrew: אלא לבתר דשתאי - ואיצטריך לאשמועינן דלא מחזקינן להו כשקרי, על אשר לא בדקוה המים:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:12:1.english: Rather, after she drank - And it was necessary to teach us that we do not presume them [the witnesses] to be liars on account of the fact that the waters did not test her.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:12:2.hebrew: שפיר - ומשום הכי לא מחזקי' להו כשקרי, דמשום דהוו ידעי בה לא בדקי לה מיא:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:12:2.english: Properly - And therefore we do not presume them to be liars, [for] because they knew about her [guilt], they did not test her with the water.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:13:1.hebrew: זכות תליא לה - דאמר לקמן (סוטה דף כ.) זכות תולה במים המרים:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:13:1.english: Merit suspends it for her - For [the Mishnah] states below (Sotah 20a) that merit suspends [the effect of] the bitter waters.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:14:1.english: And they disagree - Rav Sheshet and Rav Yosef.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:14:2.hebrew: במתנוונה - דקאמר לקמן (סוטה דף כב:) גבי אשה שתלה לה זכות:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:14:2.english: Regarding [the case of the woman who] wastes away - As it says below (Sotah 22b) regarding a woman for whom [the merit] suspended [the punishment].

Rashi on Sotah 6a:14:3.hebrew: זכות תולה - שלא יצבה בטנה מיד, אבל אינה יולדת לעולם, ואינה משבחת:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:14:3.english: The merit suspends - [Meaning,] that her belly will not swell immediately, but she never gives birth, and she does not bear praiseworthy [children].

Rashi on Sotah 6a:14:4.english: Rather, she progressively wastes away - She weakens and continues to weaken.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:14:5.english: By that same death - The swelling of her belly and the falling away of her thigh.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:15:1.hebrew: רב ששת סבר - לא פליגי רבנן עליה דרבי, אלא שסוף שהיא מתה באותה מיתה לחוד. אבל במתנוונה לא איפלוג, דכל מי שזכות תולה לה — מנוונה היא. וזו, הואיל ולא נתנוונה, לא תלה לה זכות; אלא שאינה ראויה ליבדק כלל משום עדים:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:15:1.english: Rav Sheshet holds - The Rabbis do not disagree with Rabbi, except [about the case where] in the end she dies by that very death alone. But regarding a [woman] who wastes away, they would not disagree, for anyone whose merit suspends [the punishment] for her — she wastes away. And this [woman], since she did not waste away, [her] merit did not suspend [the punishment] for her; rather, she is not fit to be examined at all, because of witnesses.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:15:2.hebrew: ורב יוסף סבר - ראויה ליבדק היא, אלא זכות תולה לה. ואי משום דלא נתנוונה, הא מני רבנן היא דאמור לקמן זכות תולה לה, דקסברי לא הויא מתנוונה כלל:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:15:2.english: And Rav Yosef holds - She is fit to be tested, but merit suspends [the effect of the water] for her. And if [you object] because she did not become withered, this [Mishnah] is in accordance with the Rabbis, who say below that merit suspends [the effect] for her, for they hold that she does not become withered at all.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:16:1.hebrew: מדחה אתה כח המים בפני הנשים - שלא יהו יראות מהם להודות שהיא טמאה, ולא ימחה שם הקדוש על המים:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:16:1.english: You are pushing aside the power of the water before the women - So that they will not be afraid of it [the water] and [will not] admit that she is impure, and the Holy Name will not be erased into the water.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:17:1.hebrew: ואי איתא - דיש לה עדים, לא מיבדקה השתא נמי. על ידי זו נמי איכא לעז על הטהורות ששתו כו':
Rashi on Sotah 6a:17:1.english: And if it is so - that she has witnesses [overseas], she would not be tested now either. Through this one too there would be a bad name [cast] upon the pure women who drank, etc.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:18:1.hebrew: מדזכות לא תליא - משום האי טעמא דחייש הוא ללעז על הטהורות, עדים נמי לא תלו:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:18:1.english: Since it does not depend on merit - Because of this reason, that he is concerned about slander against the pure women, [the Rabbis] also did not make [the law] depend on witnesses.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:19:1.hebrew: שמנחותיהן נשרפות - מנחות קנאות שלה, עשירית האיפה קמח שעורים, נשרפות למטה על בית הדשן, שאינן ראויות ליקרב, ולא לפדות וליצא לחולין:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:19:1.english: Whose meal-offerings are burned - Her jealousy meal-offerings, a tenth of an ephah of barley flour, are burned below, at the place of the ash-heap, for they are not fit to be offered, nor to be redeemed and go out to non-sacred status.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:1:1.hebrew: מי קא רמינן עליה - למינסבה בעל כרחיה? דאילו ליבם, אמרינן ליה: מצות יבום קודמת למצות חליצה. אבל בהא, אסור למימר ליה. וממילא אשמועינן קרא דאסור ליבמה, דלא שייך בה יבום, והויא כאשת אח שלא במקום מצוה:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:1:1.english: Are we imposing it upon him - to marry her against his will? For with regard to a yavam, we say to him: The mitzvah of yibbum takes precedence over the mitzvah of chalitzah. But in this case, it is forbidden to say that to him. And [so] the verse teaches us, by implication, that it is forbidden for the yavam to marry her, since yibbum does not apply to her, and she is [thus] like the wife of a brother not in a case of a mitzvah.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:2:1.hebrew: הכתוב קראו אחר - למי שנושאה. ואת אמרת תתיבם ותרמי עליה בעל כרחיה:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:2:1.english: The verse called him "another" - [This refers] to the one who marries her. But you say that she should enter levirate marriage, and you would thereby impose [the levir] upon her against her will?

Rashi on Sotah 6a:3:1.hebrew: נישאת לאחר - שגרשה ראשון שמצא בה ערות דבר, וניסת כו', לא תתיבם. דהשתא נמי אחר הוא, ואין בן זוגו של ראשון אם ישאנה, וקרמית לזה עליה במצות יבום:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:3:1.english: She married another - For the first [husband] divorced her because he found in her some indecency, and she married [another] etc., [so] she should not be taken in levirate marriage. For now too he is "another," and he is not the partner of the first [husband] if he were to marry her; yet you have imposed upon this one, with regard to her, the commandment of levirate marriage.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:3:2.english: With respect to this one - [The one called] "another" is the brother of this one.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:3:3.hebrew: בשם טוב הוה קיימא - ואיכא למימר הדרה בה, ואין קרוי ״אחר״ אלא הנושאה מתוך אלמנות או גירושין על מי שקלקלה תחתיו:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:3:3.english: She was standing in a good name - And one can say that she retracted from it [her improper conduct], and one is called "another" only if he marries her after widowhood or divorce, in succession to the one under whom she acted corruptly.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:4:1.hebrew: רבא אמר - האי דקתני מתניתין ולא מתייבמת, ק"ו: דאם נאסרת בסתירה זו במותר לה — בבעלה שהיה מותר לה, ונתקלקלו עכשיו הנישואין — ליאסר עליו:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:4:1.english: Rava said - This that the Mishnah teaches "and she does not enter into levirate marriage" [is derived through] a kal vachomer: For if she becomes forbidden through this seclusion [with a man] in respect of one who is permitted to her — in respect of her husband, who was permitted to her, and the marriage has now been spoiled — so that she becomes forbidden to him:

Rashi on Sotah 6a:4:2.hebrew: באסור לה - דהיינו יבמה, שהוא אסור לה בחיי בעלה, לא כל שכן שנאסרו נשואי הראשון שלא להתייבם מכח אותן הנישואין:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:4:2.english: With [a man who is] forbidden to her - Namely, a yevama, for whom he is forbidden during her husband's lifetime. Is it not all the more so that the first marriage [i.e., the first husband's marriage] has become forbidden, so that she may not enter levirate marriage by virtue of that same marriage?

Rashi on Sotah 6a:5:1.english: Who betrothed a widow - For she is forbidden to him:

Rashi on Sotah 6a:5:2.hebrew: לא תתיבם - מכח ק"ו זה: אם נאסרה כו'. ולקמן מפרש מאי נאסרה ומאי מותר לה, הלא אסור היה מתחילתו:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:5:2.english: She shall not enter into levirate marriage - By force of this *kal vachomer* (a fortiori argument): "If she became forbidden etc." Later [the Gemara] explains what "became forbidden" means and what "permitted to her" means, [for] was it not forbidden from the outset?

Rashi on Sotah 6a:7:1.hebrew: אלא - הכי פריך: אשת כהן שנאנסה ונאסרה עליו, דאשת כהן אסורה אפילו באונס. אבל אשת ישראל מותרת, דכתיב (במדבר ה) "והיא לא נתפשה" — הא נתפשה, מותרת. ומדכתיב "והיא", מיעוטא הוא, ומשמע דיש אחרת שאפילו נתפשה אסורה:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:7:1.english: Rather - This is how [Rava] objects: [the case of] a priest's wife who was raped, and she became forbidden to him, for a priest's wife is forbidden even [when the intercourse was] through rape. But an Israelite's wife is permitted, as it is written (Numbers 5) "and she was not taken [in the act]" — [which implies that] if she was taken [by force], she is permitted. And since it is written "and she," it is a limitation, and it implies that there is another [woman] who is forbidden even if she was taken [by force].

Rashi on Sotah 6a:7:2.hebrew: ויש לו אחיו - מאביו, והוא חלל שנולד לאביו מן הגרושה, ונתחלל מן הכהונה, ומותר בנשים הפסולות לכהונה, כדכתיב בכהנים הנושאין פסולות: ולא יחלל זרעו (ויקרא כא), אלמא זרעו חלל:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:7:2.english: And he has a brother - From his father; and he is a *chalal* who was born to his father from a divorcée, and was disqualified from the priesthood, and is permitted to marry women who are disqualified from the priesthood, as it is written regarding priests who marry disqualified women: "And he shall not profane his offspring" (Leviticus 21). Evidently, his offspring is profaned.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:7:3.hebrew: לא תתיבם - מק"ו זה: אם נאסרה בבעילה זו לבעלה, שהיה מותר לה, ביבמה, האסור לה באותה שעה, לא כל שכן שנאסרו עליו נישואי אחיו, שלא ליבמה מכח נשואין:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:7:3.english: She shall not enter into levirate marriage - From this *kal vachomer* (a fortiori argument): If through this act of intercourse she became forbidden to her husband, who was permitted to her, then with regard to her *yavam* (levir), who is forbidden to her at that time, all the more so that the marriage of his brother has become forbidden to him, so that he may not perform levirate marriage with her by virtue of that marriage.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:8:1.english: There is no prohibition - And for him it is entirely permitted, and this is not a *kal vachomer*. But where she committed adultery willingly, in which the husband and the yavam are equal with regard to this prohibition, if she was under him it is a *kal vachomer*: for it is by virtue of the first marriage that she is bound to yibbum, and if she was rendered defiled with respect to the husband, [it is] a *kal vachomer* with respect to the yavam.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:9:1.english: From eating terumah - If he is a priest.

Rashi on Sotah 6a:9:2.hebrew: ושבעלה בא עליה בדרך - דשוב אין המים בודקין אותה, כדלקמן (סוטה דף כח.): ״ונקה האיש מעון״ — בזמן שהאיש מנוקה, שלא בא עליה מאחר שנאסרה עליו, אז ״האשה ההיא תשא את עונה״; אין האיש מנוקה מעון — אין המים בודקין את אשתו:
Rashi on Sotah 6a:9:2.english: And that her husband had relations with her on the way - For then the water no longer tests her, as is stated below (Sotah 28a): "And the man shall be clear of iniquity" — when the man is clear, meaning that he did not have relations with her after she became forbidden to him, then "that woman shall bear her iniquity"; if the man is not clear of iniquity, the water does not test his wife.

Tosafot on Sotah 6a:11:1.hebrew: ושבאו לה עדים ואמרו שנטמאה - מספקא לרבי: אי דוקא נקט עדים — שנים, אבל עד אחד לא מהימן, דמוקמינן ליה בגמרא דמיירי לאחר ששתתה, דדוקא קודם ששתתה האמינה תורה לעד אחד; ורב ששת דאמר בגמרא "סוטה שיש לה עדים במדינת הים — דאין המים בודקין אותה", דוקא עדים נקט, ולא עד א'. או דילמא כיון דהאמינה תורה לעד אחד אחר קינוי וסתירה, ליכא חילוק בין אחד לשנים. מיהו מסתברא דה"ה לעד אחד, כדעולא דאמר בפרק מי שאמר (לקמן סוטה דף לא:): כל מקום שהאמינה תורה עד אחד, הרי כאן שנים:
Tosafot on Sotah 6a:11:1.english: "And witnesses came and said that she had become defiled" - Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] is uncertain whether the Mishnah specifically means witnesses — two — but one witness is not believed, since we establish it in the Gemara as dealing with [a case] after she has drunk, for the Torah believed a single witness only before she drank; and Rav Sheshet, who said in the Gemara, "A sotah who has witnesses overseas — the water does not test her," specifically said witnesses, and not one witness. Or perhaps, since the Torah believed a single witness after the warning and the seclusion, there is no distinction between one and two. Nevertheless, it is reasonable that the same applies to a single witness, in accordance with Ulla, who said in the chapter Mi She'amar (below, Sotah 31b): Wherever the Torah believed a single witness, it is as if there are two here.

Tosafot on Sotah 6a:16:1.hebrew: אם אתה אומר זכות תולה מדחה אתה את המים - וא"ת, לרב ששת דאמר בין לרבי בין לרבנן מתנוונה, א"כ אהיכא קאי ר"ש דאמר "מדחה אתה"? והלא יראו דמתנוונת, והיאך יוכלו להוציא שם רע על הטהורות ששתו כשלא יתנוונו? יש לומר: הנשים העומדות משום ייסור, ולא יהא ניכר לאלתר כשעומדת בעזרה; נתנוונה — יוציאו שם רע, והבועל יגיד להם שקלקל עמה, ולא ידעי שזו מתנוונת. אי נמי, לא יתלו נוונווה במים המרים, וכן היא לא תתלה במים המרים אלא בחולי אחר:
Tosafot on Sotah 6a:16:1.english: "If you say that merit suspends [the punishment], you are rejecting the water" - And if you ask: According to Rav Sheshet, who said that whether according to Rabbi or according to the Rabbis she wastes away, then to what case does Rabbi Shimon refer when he says, "you are rejecting the water"? Surely people would see that she wastes away, so how could they cast an evil reputation on the pure women who drank, if those women do not waste away? One can answer: [In the case of] the women who stand [there] for the sake of chastisement, it will not be immediately noticeable when she stands in the Temple court. [If] she wastes away — they will cast an evil reputation [on her], and the paramour will tell them that he sinned with her, and [people] will not know that this woman is one who wastes away. Alternatively, they will not attribute her wasting away to the bitter water, and she herself will likewise not attribute it to the bitter water, but to some other illness.

Tosafot on Sotah 6a:1:1.hebrew: מי קא רמינן עליה בעל כרחיה - הכא הוה מצי למיפרך כדפריך לבסוף, דאמר: "אלא מעתה נשאת לאחר ומת בלא בנים לא תתייבם", דלא נסתריה לביתיה:
Tosafot on Sotah 6a:1:1.english: "Are we imposing it upon him against his will?" - Here [Abaye] could have objected as he objects at the end, when he says: "But if so, if she married another and he died without children, she should not be subject to yibbum," since he did not seclude her in his house.

Tosafot on Sotah 6a:7:1.hebrew: אשת כהן שנאנסה - וא"ת: אמאי לא תני לה בפרק "יש מותרות" (יבמות דף פד.) גבי "אסורות לבעליהן ומותרות ליבמיהן"? יש לומר: הא תני ליה "חייבי לאוין", וזו מחייבי לאוין, כדאמר בפרק "הבא על יבמתו" (יבמות דף נו:): הכל היו בכלל "אחרי אשר הוטמאה" וגו'. והכי מתרץ התם דפריך מפצוע דכא. אבל יש לתמוה: אמאי לא פריך הכא, ישראל שנשא כשרה ונעשה פצוע דכא, ויש לו אח כשר, דדמי למתני' — מאי הוי ליה לתרוצי:
Tosafot on Sotah 6a:7:1.english: The wife of a priest who was raped - And if you ask: Why doesn't [the Mishnah] teach this case in the chapter "Yesh Muterot" (Yevamot 84a), among [those women] who are forbidden to their husbands but permitted to their brothers-in-law [i.e., to a yavam]? One can answer: It already teaches it there under "those liable for [violating] a negative commandment," and this [woman] is among those liable for a negative commandment, as it says in the chapter "HaBa al Yevimto" (Yevamot 56b): All of them were included in the verse "after she was defiled," etc. And so [the Gemara] answers there, where it challenges from [the case of] one whose testicles were crushed. But it is astonishing: Why doesn't [the Gemara] challenge here [with the case of] an Israelite who married a fit woman and then became one whose testicles were crushed, and he has a fit brother, which is similar to our Mishnah? What would [the Gemara] have had to answer?

Tosafot on Sotah 6a:9:1.hebrew: האומרת טמאה אני לך - אי קשיא בשלהי מסכת נדרים (דף צ:), דפליגי רבה ורב ששת באומרת "טמאה אני לך": דרב ששת אומר אוכלת בתרומה וכו'. תריץ: דהכא מיירי אחר קינוי וסתירה, דרגלים לדבר, אפילו רב ששת מודה. והכי מפרש לה בירושלמי:
Tosafot on Sotah 6a:9:1.english: "She who says, 'I am impure to you'" - If it is difficult: at the end of tractate Nedarim (90b), Rabbah and Rav Sheshet disagree about a woman who says "I am impure to you"; for Rav Sheshet says she may eat terumah, etc. Answer: Here [the Mishnah] is speaking of [a case] after warning and seclusion, where there is circumstantial evidence supporting [her claim]; even Rav Sheshet agrees. And so it is explained in the Jerusalem Talmud.
